1.1  Cabinet Approves Two Semiconductor Manufacturing Units Worth Rs. 3,900 crore under ISMp.6
Exam Hints:
  • Approval: Two semiconductor projects
  • Project 1: India’s first commercial GaN (Gallium Nitride) Technology-based Mini/Micro-LED (Light Emitting Diode) display facility by Crystal Matrix Limited (CML)
  • Project 2: Semiconductor packaging unit by Suchi Semicon Private Limited (SSPL).
  • Investment: Rs. 3,936 Crore.
  • State: Gujarat.
  • Nodal Mission: India Semiconductor Mission (ISM).
  • Total ISM Projects: 12.
  • Cumulative Investment: Rs.1.64 Lakh Crore.
Crystal Matrix Limited Project:
  • Capacity: Manufacture Mini/Micro-LED display modules and GaN (Gallium Nitride) foundry services with 6-inch wafer epitaxy, producing 72,000 square meters (Sq.m) of Mini/Micro-LED panels and 24,000 RGB (Red Green Blue) GaN wafer sets annually.
Strategic Milestone:
  • ISM 1.0
  • Overview: ISM 1.0 is a specialised division under the Digital India Corporation under MeitY, launched in December 2021 with an outlay of Rs. 76,000 crore to build a self-reliant semiconductor and display manufacturing ecosystem in India.
  • Global Role: India hosts around 7% of the world’s semiconductor Global Capability Centres (GCCs) and nearly 20% of the global semiconductor design workforce.
ISM 2.0:
  • Expansion: Announced in the Union Budget 2026–27, ISM 2.0 expands focus from fabs and OSAT units to semiconductor equipment, materials, indigenous Intellectual Property (IP), and Research and Development (R&D) centres, with an initial allocation of ₹1,000 crore.

1.2  Cabinet Approves ECLGS 5.0 with Outlay of Rs 18,100 Crorep.7
Exam Hints:
  • What: Cabinet approved ECLGS 5.0
  • Outlay: Rs 18,100 Cr
  • Purpose: Credit guarantee coverage:
  • 100% for MSMEs
  • 90% for non-MSMEs, Airline Sector
  • Provided to: Member Lending Institutions (MLIs)
  • Administration: NCGTC
  • Eligible Borrowers: MSMEs and non-MSMEs, Airlines with existing working capital as of March 31, 2026
  • Duration: Up to 31.03.2027
  • Credit Flow: Rs 2.55 lakh Cr (For airline – Rs 5000 Cr)
  • Interest Rate: Banks-9%, NBFCs-13% or 0.75% above benchmark rate
  • Loan Tenure: MSMEs & Non-MSMEs: 5 years, moratorium – 1 yearAirline Sector: 7 years, moratorium – 2 yearGuarantee: Aligned with loan tenure
Key Features:
  • Duration: Scheme would be applicable to all loans sanctioned during the period from the date of issue of these guidelines by NCGTC up to 31.03.2027.
  • Guarantee coverage: 100% for MSMEs and 90% for non-MSMEs as well as the airline sector.
  • Credit Flow: The scheme will target additional credit flow of Rs 2.55 lakh Cr including Rs 5,000 Cr for airlines.
  • Additional Credit: MSME and non-MSME units can access additional credit of up to 20% of their peak working capital utilised during Quarter 4 Financial Year 2026 (Q4 FY26: January – March 2026), with a cap set at Rs 100 Cr per unit.Scheduled passenger airlines can borrow up to 100% of outstanding credit facilities, capped at Rs 1,500 per borrower.
  • Interest Rate: The rate of interest by banks will be capped at 9% and by non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) would be 13% or 0.75% above benchmark rate, whichever is lower.
About Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS):
  • Launched: ECLGS was launched in May 2020 as part of the Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyaan.

1.3  CCEA Approves Major Infrastructure, Railway & Judicial Expansion Proposals on May 5, 2026p.8
Exam Hints:
  • What: Major Infrastructure, Railway & Judicial Expansion Proposals approved by CCEA
  • Approval-1: Development of Ship Repair Facility
  • Location: Vadinar in Devbhumi Dwarka district (Gujarat)
  • Investment: Rs 1,570 crore
  • Implementing Agencies: DPA and CSL
  • Key Components: 650 m long jetty, two large floating dry docks, workshops
  • Approval-2: 3 Rail Multi-Tracking Projects
  • Investment: Rs 23,437 crore
  • Coverage: 19 districts of 6 states (MP, Rajasthan, UP, Karnataka, AP and Telangana)
  • Rail Lines: Nagda-Mathura 3rd and 4th Line, Guntakal-Wadi 3rd and 4th Line, and Burhwal-Sitapur 3rd and 4th Line
  • Approval-3: Increase Strength of SC Judges to 37
  • Existing Strength: 33 (in 2019)
  • Expansion Through: Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026
  • Constitutional Provision: Article 124 (1).
About Rs 1,570 crore Ship Repair facility:
  • Implementation: The project will be jointly implemented by Deendayal Port Authority (DPA) and Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL) with a total investment of Rs 1,570 crore.
  • Maritime Vision: The initiative will boost regional economic growth and support India’s long-term maritime goals under Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047.
Railway Projects Across 6 States:
  • Approval: CCEA chaired by PM Narendra Modi approved 3 railway projects covering 19 districts across 6 states: Madhya Pradesh (MP), Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh (UP), Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh (AP) and Telangana, with an estimated cost of Rs 23,437 crore.
Expansion of SC Judge Strength to 37:
  • Revision of SC Judges Strength: Initially, the strength of SC Judges was capped at 8 (including CJI), but, later, the number was increased through successive amendments i.e. from 10 judges (in 1956) to 13 (in 1960), 17 (in 1977), 25 (in 1986) and 30 (in 2008) to 33 (in 2019).
About Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL):
  • Chairman and Managing Director (CMD)- Jose V J (Additional Charge)
  • Headquarters: Kochi, Kerala
  • Established: 1972

1.4  Cabinet Approves Rs 365 per quintal FRP for Sugarcane for 2026-27 Seasonp.10
Exam Hints:
  • What: Approval of FRP for Sugarcane for 2026-27 Season
  • Approved by: CCEA
  • Revised FRP: Rs.365 per quintal (+2.81%)
  • Basic Sugar Recovery Rate: 10.25%
  • Effective From: October 01, 2026
  • Other Approval: Mission for Cotton Productivity
  • Budget Outlay: Rs 5659.22 crore
  • Implementation Period: 2026-27 to 2030-31
  • Aligns with: 5F vision
  • Implementing Agencies: MoAFW, MoT and other institutions.
Background:
  • The revised FRP marks an increase of 2.81% compared to Rs 355 per quintal for the current season (2025-26).
Key Details:
  • Deduction: Further, no deduction will be made for sugar mills where recovery is below 9.5% with such farmers to be paid Rs 338.30 per quintal in the 2026-27 season.
Cabinet Approves Mission for Cotton Productivity:
  • Approval: Union Cabinet chaired by PM Narendra Modi, approved ‘Mission for Cotton Productivity (2026-27 to 2030-31)’ with total budget outlay of Rs 5659.22 crore.India’s cotton season is observed annually from October to September.
  • Key Target: Mission is expected to achieve the production of 498 lakh bales (170 kilogram (kg) lint each) of cotton by increasing lint productivity from 440 kg per hectare (ha) to 755 kg per ha by 2031.Further, the mission is expected to benefit nearly 32 lakh farmers leading to self-reliance.
About Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP):
  • Background: It was initially established as the Agricultural Prices Commission on January 08, 1965 and was later renamed as CACP on March 18, 1985.
  • Chairman: Prof. Vijay Paul Sharma

1.5  Cabinet Approves Rs 37,500 Crore Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification Projectsp.11
Exam Hints:
  • What: Approval of Scheme for promotion of surface coal/lignite gasification projects
  • Approved by: Union Cabinet, chaired by PM Narendra Modi
  • Total Budget Outlay: Rs 37,500 crore
  • Gasification Target: 75 MT of coal/lignite
  • National Target: 100 MT coal gasification by 2030
  • Based on: National Coal Gasification Mission (NCGM)
  • Maximum Incentive: Up to 20% of plant & machinery cost
  • Coal Linkage Tenure: Up to 30 years
  • Expected Investment: Rs.2.5–3 lakh crore.
About Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification Projects:
  • Disbursement of Incentive: Under the scheme, incentive will be disbursed in four equal instalments, linked to project milestones.GoI has capped the financial incentive for any single project at Rs.5,000 crore; for any single product (excluding SNG and Urea) at Rs.9,000 crore; and any single entity group at Rs.12,000 crore across all projects.
  • Key Target: With the approval of the new scheme, the Government of India (GoI) is targeting gasification of nearly 75 Million Tonnes (MT) of coal and lignite, accelerating the national target of gasifying 100 MT of coal by 2030.
Economic and Strategic Benefits:
  • Employment Generation: It is estimated to generate nearly 50,000 direct and indirect jobs across 25 projects in coal-bearing regions.
About National Coal Gasification Mission (NCGM):
  • Launch: NCGM was launched in 2021, and in January 2024, the Union Cabinet approved an incentive package worth Rs.8,500 crore for the mission.
  • Key Progress: Under NCGM, currently, 8 projects worth Rs 6,233 crore are under implementation.

1.7  Cabinet Approves Ahmedabad–Dholera Rail Project; Nagpur International Airport Modernisationp.14
Exam Hints:
  • What: Cabinet Approvals on Rail Projects and Airport Modernization
  • Approval 1: Project: Approval of 134 km Ahmedabad–Dholera Semi High-Speed Rail ProjectBy whom: CCEA chaired by PM Narendra ModiMinistry: Ministry of RailwaysProject Cost: Rs 20,667 croreWhere: GujaratCompletion Target: 2030-31
  • Approval 2: What: Modernisation of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport under PPP modelBy whom: Union Cabinet chaired by PM Narendra ModiWhere: Nagpur, MaharashtraPPP Operator: GNIAL a subsidiary of GMR Airports LimitedConcession Period: 30 years
Background:
  • Union Cabinet approved extension of Airports Authority of India (AAI) land lease to MIHAN India Limited (MIL) beyond August 2039, enabling GMR Nagpur International Airport Limited (GNIAL) to operate and modernise Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport, Nagpur Maharashtra.
About the Approval of Ahmedabad–Dholera Semi High-Speed Rail Project:
  • Approval: CCEA approved the project under the Ministry of Railways (MoR) at an estimated cost of Rs.20,667 crore with completion targeted by 2030–31.
  • Coverage: The project will increase the Indian Railways network by about 134 km and improve connectivity for nearly 284 villages with a beneficiary population of around 5 lakh people.
About the Approval of Nagpur International Airport Modernisation:
  • Operation: The airport will be operated by GNIAL for 30 years from the Commercial Operation Date (COD) under a long-term concession agreement.
  • Framework: MIL, formed in 2009 as a joint venture between AAI with 49% equity and Maharashtra Airport Development Company Limited (MADC) with 51%, manages the project framework, while GNIAL was selected through a global tender process.
Airports Authority of India (AAI) - Static GK:

Headquarters: New Delhi, Delhi

1.8  Cabinet Approves Rs.25,530 Crore SARTHAK-PDS Scheme for 5 years and Merges Two Existing Schemes to Modernise PDSp.15
Exam Hints:
  • What: Approval for extension of SARTHAK-PDS Scheme
  • By Whom: CCEA, chaired by PM Narendra Modi
  • Implementation: DFPD under MoCAF&PD.
  • Scheme Tenure: 5 years till March 2031
  • Outlay: Rs. 25,530 crore (Central share)
  • Beneficiaries: 81.35 crore NFSA beneficiaries
  • Merged Schemes: Assistance to State Agencies for intra-State movement of foodgrains and FPS dealers’ margin under NFSA & SMART PDS
  • Tech Focus: AI, ML, NLP, Blockchain-based PDS digitisation
  • AI-Powered Platforms: NIRMAL (registry), ASHA (grievance AI), SAKSHAM (logistics AI)
About SARTHAK-PDS Scheme:
  • Implementation: The scheme is implemented by the Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD) under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution (MoCAF&PD).
  • Coverage: The scheme covers 81.35 crore beneficiaries under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013 across all 36 States and Union Territories (UTs), supporting India’s food and nutritional security commitment.
  • Benefits: The scheme is expected to reduce logistics costs by 15–50%, save nearly Rs.280 crore annually, lower carbon emissions by about 36% and improve delivery efficiency and grievance handling.
About the Existing PDS Reform Schemes:
  • Assistance Scheme: The “Assistance to State Agencies for intra-State movement of foodgrains and Fair Price Shop (FPS) dealers’ margin under NFSA Act, 2013, is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) launched on 25 March 2015 by CCEA, implemented by DFPD, MoCAF&PD to ensure that intra-state transport and FPS dealer margin costs do not increase foodgrain prices for beneficiaries.

  • Budget & Phases: Approved with an outlay of Rs.2,000 crore over two years Phase I: 2024–2026; Phase II is planned to run from 2026 to 2031.

1.12  Union Minister Nitin Gadkari Launches India’s First Barrier-less Tolling System in Gujaratp.19
Exam Hints:
  • Event: India’s first Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) Toll System launched
  • Launched by: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari, MoRTH
  • Location: Chorayasi Toll Plaza, NH-48, Gujarat
  • Core Technologies: ANPR; RFID (FASTag)
  • Primary Benefit: Elimination of toll plazas and traffic congestion.
About First Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF):
  • Technology: The system enables barrier-free tolling using integrated technologies such as ANPR (Automatic Number Plate Recognition) withArtificial intelligence (AI) analytics and RFID (Radio Frequency Identification)-based Electronic Toll Collection (FASTag).
  • Benefits: Under the barrier-less model, toll charges are automatically deducted from linked accounts, enabling contactless, seamless transactions while reducing fuel use, emissions, and travel time.
  • Impact: The initiative supports India’s push for digital infrastructure and smart mobility, aiming to build a more efficient, user-friendly road transport system nationwide.

Highlights of the event:

About Cell Broadcast System (CBS):

About National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA):
  • Background: NDMA, an apex body for disaster management in India, was initially set up on May 30, 2005, under the chairmanship of the Prime Minister (PM) by an executive order.
  • Established: 2005

1.15  MoHFW Releases Guidance Document on Diabetes Mellitus in Childrenp.21
Exam Hints:
  • What: Release of Guidance Document on Diabetes Mellitus in Children
  • Released by: MoHFW
  • Where: During National Summit on Best Practices in Public Healthcare, Chandigarh
  • Screening Age: From birth to 18 years
  • Framework: 4Ts (Toilet, Thirsty, Tired, and Thinner)
  • Key Features: Free Care Package and Integrated Care.
Background:
  • The newly released document is India’s 1st structured and standardised national framework for the screening, diagnosis, treatment and long-term management of diabetes in children.
Types:
  • Type-1 diabetes: It is an autoimmune condition in which the body produces little or no insulin.Type-2 diabetes: It is a condition where high blood sugar levels result from the body’s inability to produce enough insulin or use it properly.
About Childhood Diabetes Framework:
  • Objective: To ensure universal diabetes screening of all children from birth to 18 years, using both community and school platforms for early detection.
  • 4Ts Framework: It introduces the ‘4Ts awareness framework- Toilet, Thirsty, Tired and Thinner’, for early detection of Type 1 Diabetes among children.
About Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW):
  • Union Minister: Jagat Prakash (JP) Nadda (Rajya Sabha – Gujarat) Minister of State (MoS)- Anupriya Patel (Constituency- Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh, UP); Jadhav Prataprao Ganpatrao (Constituency- Buldhana, Maharashtra)

1.16  NITI Aayog Launches CPO Portal for Real-Time Governance and Last-Mile Deliveryp.22
Exam Hints:
  • What: Central Prabhari Officer (CPO) Portal launched
  • By whom: Nidhi Chhibber, interim CEO, NITI Aayog
  • Programme linked: Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) & Aspirational Blocks Programme (ABP)
  • Purpose: Real-time governance and last-mile delivery improvement.
Background:
  • The platform aims to bridge the gap between field-level observations and administrative action through a structured real-time reporting system.
About CPO Portal:
  • Officers: CPOs are senior Central Government officials responsible for providing ground-level insights, monitoring programme implementation, and strengthening coordination between Centre, State, and District administrations.
  • Functionality: CPOs can upload real-time field observations and implementation issues through mobile devices, enabling authorities to monitor, access, and respond simultaneously.
  • Coordination: The platform enables State Planning Secretaries to monitor inter-departmental coordination and implementation progress, while districts can take corrective actions and provide feedback in real time.
  • Governance: The portal strengthens structured monitoring, accountability, faster administrative response, and technology-driven inclusive governance across Aspirational Districts and Blocks.

  • Sub-sectors Classification: 6 segments (capital goods manufacturing, electronic capital goods and components, advanced battery components, among others)
  • Reporting Process Governed under: Foreign Exchange Management (Mode of Payment and Reporting of Non-debt Instruments) Regulations, 2019.
Background:
  • As per the updated SOP, FDI proposals from countries like: China, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar, and Afghanistan in these sub-sectors will be processed within 60 days.
Key Details:
  • Classification: The 40 sub-sectors fall under 6 main segments, including capital goods manufacturing, electronic capital goods and components, advanced battery components, polysilicon and wafers, rare earth processing, and rare earth permanent magnets.
  • Reporting: GoI has clarified the reporting under the new guidelines will be administered under the Foreign Exchange Management (Mode of Payment and Reporting of Non-debt Instruments) Regulations, 2019 and the information will be accessible by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).Further, the responsibility for reporting entrusted on the Indian investee company, which now requires to submit important details to the DPIIT before receiving foreign capital.

About Plant-OpenCRISPR1:
  • Objective: The platform aims to develop climate-resilient, disease-resistant, high-yield, and nutritionally enhanced crop varieties by enabling precise genome editing without introducing foreign genes.

1.78  Govt Expands GATC Framework to Include 5 types of fuel dispensers verificationp.80
Exam Hints:
  • Framework: Legal Metrology (Government Approved Test Centre) Amendment Rules, 2026.
  • Nodal Ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution.
  • Expansion: Total GATC-verifiable asset categories increased from 18 to 23.
  • New Inclusions (5): Dispensers for Petrol/Diesel, CNG, LPG, LNG, and Hydrogen.
  • Verification Fee: Rs. 5,000 per nozzle for Petrol and Diesel; Rs. 10,000 per nozzle for green/gas alternatives (CNG, LPG, LNG, Hydrogen).
  • Global Alignment: Harmonized with the International Organization of Legal Metrology (OIML) guidelines.
  • Significance: To enhance efficiency and support the growing adoption of cleaner fuels across India.
Background:
  • Under the amended rules, GATCs are now authorised to verify five additional fuel dispensing systems, including Petrol/Diesel, Compressed Natural Gas (CNG), Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG), Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG), and Hydrogen.
Key Details of Legal Metrology Amendment Rules, 2026:
  • Expansion: This Amendment expands the scope of GATCs to include verification and re-verification of additional fuel dispensing systems, increasing coverage from 18 to 23 categories of weights and measures under the Legal Metrology framework.
Fee Structure:
  • Legal Metrology Rules, 2013: The 2026 Amendment introduces a standardised fee structure under the Fifth Schedule, setting uniform costs per nozzle to ensure consistency across testing regimes.Hydrocarbons: The verification fee for Petrol and Diesel dispensers is fixed at Rs. 5,000 per nozzle.Clean & Alternative Fuels: Reflecting higher technological complexity, pressure requirements, and safety standards, the verification fee for CNG, LPG, LNG, and Hydrogen dispensers is set at Rs.10,000 per nozzle.

  • Impact: The initiative improves access to justice in remote and hilly areas, while reducing administrative costs and environmental impact through paperless operations.

6.1  RBI Eases Rules for Small NBFCs, Grants Exemptions from July 1, 2026p.133
Exam Hints:
  • Released by: RBI
  • Effective From: 1 July 2026
  • Type I NBFC: No public funds; No customer interface & Assets < Rs.1,000 crore
  • Classification: Type I (Unregistered) & Type II (Others)
  • Deregistration: Via PRAVAAH portal by 31 Dec 2026 Framework 2: Loan Resolution in calamities
  • Released by: RBI
  • Effective from: 1 July 2026
  • Applicability: NDRF & SDRF
  • Opt-Out Window: 135 days
  • Provisioning: 5% additional
  • Timeline: Invoke – 45 days; Implement – 90 days.
Background:
  • The regulations come into effect from July 1, 2026.
  • RBI issues directions to banks and non-bank lenders to implement suo motu resolution for borrowers affected by natural calamities.
RBI Framework for Unregistered Type I NBFCs:
  • One-time window: Existing NBFCs meeting these criteria given a one-time window to apply for deregistration by December 31, 2026, introducing, for the first time, a structured exit route from the regulatory framework.The deregistration application is to be made through the RBI’s PRAVAAH (Platform for Regulatory Application, Validation And AutHorisation) portal.
RBI Allows Banks to Implement Suo Motu Loan Resolution in Calamities:
  • In April 2026, the RBI issued directions in which it has allowed banks and non-bank lenders to implement suo motu resolution for borrowers affected by natural calamities on the recommendation of the State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC).The revised rules will come into effect from 1 July 2026.
  • Timeline: RBI instructed that resolution must be invoked within 45 days of the calamity declaration and implemented within 90 days thereafter.

Exam Hints:
  • What: Removal of RBI approval requirement

  • Through: AD Category-I banks
  • Coverage: Cross-border outward remittances for non-trade current account transactions.
Background:
  • This direction is part of the operating framework issued by RBI to facilitate outward remittance services by non-bank entities through Authorised Dealer (AD) Category-I banks in India.
Key Details:
  • Previous Arrangement: Under the previous 2016 framework, non-bank entities were mandated to obtain RBI approval before entering into tie-up arrangements with AD banks in India, for outward remittance services.
  • Applicability: The updated framework will be applicable to cross-border outward remittance of funds for non trade current account transactions facilitated via websites, online platforms, software applications (apps), and mobile apps operated by 3rd-party entities.
  • Compliance: As per RBI directions, AD banks mandated to adhere to the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA) and perform due diligence through Know Your Customer (KYC).

6.5  RBI Amends Directions on IFR for Various Bank Categoriesp.136
Exam Hints:
  • What: RBI revises IFR framework
  • CB & FB: Discontinued W.e.f May 18, 2026
  • IFR Transfer: Statutory Reserve, General Reserve, Balance of P&L for CB
  • For FB – transferred to Statutory Reserve/ retained surplus in Indian Books
  • Tier 1 Capital: IFR treated as Tier 1 for CB and FB
  • PB, SFB, RRB: IFR of atleast 2% of AFS and FVTPL
  • Eligible for Tier 2 capital classification
  • UCB: IFR of 5%, Tier 2 Capital
  • RCB: IFR of 5%
Key Highlights:
  • IFR Discontinuation: Under the revised norms, the requirement of IFR discontinued with effect from May 18, 2026.
Other Regulated Entities:
  • PB, SFB, RRB: A bank shall create an IFR out of the realised gains on sale of investments, subject to the availability of net profit, until the balance in IFR is at least 2% of the Available For Sale (AFS) and Fair Value through Profit and Loss (FVTPL) (including Held For Trading (HFT)) portfolio.The balance in IFR shall be eligible for inclusion in Tier 2 capital.These directions are applicable to Payment Banks (PB), Small Finance Banks (SFB) and Regional Rural Bank (RRB).
  • Urban Cooperative Bank (UCB): A UCB shall maintain a minimum IFR of 5% of the investment portfolio.A UCB may, at its discretion, transfer the IFR amount exceeding 5% of its AFS and HFT investments to the Profit and Loss Account at the end of an accounting year.IFR shall be eligible for inclusion in Tier 2 capital.
About Reserve Bank of India:
  • It was established on 1st April 1935 in accordance with the provisions of the RBI Act,1934.

6.8  RBI Declared Rs 2.87 lakh Crore Dividend to GoI for FY26p.138
Exam Hints:
  • What: RBI Approval to transfer dividend to GoI for FY26
  • Surplus Transfer: Rs 2,86,588.46 crore
  • Approved at: 623rd meeting of CBoD of RBI
  • CRB Approved: Rs 1,09,379.64 crore
Background:
  • The decision to transfer the dividend was taken during the 623rd meeting of the Central Board of Directors (CBoDs) of RBI, chaired by Dr. Sanjay Malhotra, Governor of RBI in Mumbai, Maharashtra.
Key Details:
  • Expansion of Balance Sheet: As on March 31 2026, the balance sheet of RBI expanded by 20.61% to Rs 91.97 lakh crore.
  • Income and Expenditure: The gross income of RBI has increased by 26.42% over the last financial year while its expenditure before risk provisions surged by 27.60%.
  • Transfer towards CRB: Considering macroeconomic conditions, financial performance and risk management requirements, the board of central bank approved a transfer of Rs 1,09,379.64 crore towards the Contingency Risk Buffer (CRB) for FY26 (up from Rs 44, 861.70 crore allocated in the previous year), maintaining CRB at 6.5% of the RBI’s balance sheet.As per the revised Economic Capital Framework (ECB), RBI is required to maintain CRB within a range of 4.5% to 7.5% of the balance sheet size.

About RBI Penalties:
  • CUB: RBI imposed a penalty of Rs 10.10 lakh on CUB, an Indian private sector bank, for levying loan-related charges on certain priority sector agriculture advances up to Rs 25,000 and for failing to report Self Help Group (SHG) member-level data to credit information companies.
  • Mintifi Finserve: A penalty of Rs 3.10 lakh was imposed on Mintifi Finserve, a Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC), for failure to upload certain customers’ Know Your Customer (KYC) records to the Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR) within the prescribed timeline.
  • Newa Investments: RBI imposed a penalty of Rs 2.70 lakh on Newa Investments, a NBFC, for appointing directors without prior RBI approval, leading to a management change involving over 30% of directors.

6.10  RBI Mandates 3 year cooling-off period for UCB, RCB directors, Sets up committee to examine quantum tech in Financep.140
Exam Hints:
  • What: RBI amends directions for UCBs, RCBs director cooling-off period
  • Period: 3 years after completing 10 years tenure
  • Restrictions: During the cooling period – direction shall not be associated with the same bank
  • Tenure Reset: Gap of 3 years only restarts the tenure clock Expert Committee
  • Purpose: Examine the opportunities and risks arising from quantum tech in finance sector
  • Initiative: Q-SAFE
  • Members: 8, chaired by: Dr Anil Prabhakar
Key Highlights:
  • Sections: The amendments, issued under Section 35A read with Section 10A (2A)(i) and Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
  • Background: The ceiling on continuous tenure of directors for co-operative banks came into force for UCBs from June 29, 2020 and for State Co-operative banks (StCB) and Central Co-operative banks (CCB) from April 1, 2021.Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 subsequently increased the maximum continuous tenure for directors from 8 years to 10 years effective August 1, 2025.
  • Amendment: As per the latest amendment, directors completing a continuous tenure of 10 years on the board of a UCB, StCB or CCB will be eligible for re-appointment to the same bank’s board only after undergoing a minimum cooling-off period of 3 years.
  • Restrictions: During the 3 year cooling off period, the former director shall not be associated with the same bank in any capacity or manner other than as a member or customer.

6.23  MoF Amends FEMA Rules, Allows 100% FDI in Insurance sector via Automatic routep.149
Exam Hints:
  • What: Notification of FEMA (Non-debt Instruments) (Second Amendment) Rules, 2026
  • Notified by: MoF
  • Implication: 100% FDI in Insurance Sector via Automatic Route
  • Comply with: Insurance Act, 1938
  • Applicable: Insurance brokers, reinsurance brokers, insurance consultants, corporate agents, among others
  • Exception: Retains FDI in LIC at 20%.
Background:
  • MoF in exercise of the powers conferred by clauses (aa) and (ab) of sub-section (2) of section 46 of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, (FEMA, 1999) (42 of 1999), amended the FEMA (Non-debt instruments) Rules, 2019.
Key Details:
  • FDI Limit: Under the revised norms, insurance companies can now receive up to 100% FDI via the automatic route, replacing the earlier 74% cap and eliminating the need for prior government approval.
  • Retain LIC Cap: However, MoF has clarified that foreign investment in Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) continues to be capped at 20% under the automatic route.
  • Other Conditions: The new FEMA 2026 rules outlined additional requirements for insurance intermediaries with majority foreign ownership like: incorporation as a limited company under the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 (18 of 2013), and obligations to bring in the latest technological, managerial and other skills.

About ‘RAINMUMBAI’:
  • Purpose: The new contract derivative, scheduled to be implemented on June 01, 2026, is designed to hedge the financial exposure of rainfall extremes and variability in the city of Mumbai (Maharashtra) and its surrounding area.

  • Settlement Process: The contract will be cash-settled, with data sourced from IMD surface rainfall observations and Automatic Weather Stations (AWSs) located in Santa Cruz and Colaba.
  • Data Period: The benchmark for new contract derivative built using a 30 year rainfall dataset i.e. from 1991 to 2020.

  • Average Global Prices: The report highlighted that globally, the direct carbon prices have increased 7% compared to last year’s report and have nearly doubled over the last 10 years i.e. from USD 10 per tonne of Carbon Dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) (in 2016) to nearly USD21 per tCO2e (in 2026)
  • Credit Issuances: As per the report, carbon credit issuances increased 8% between 2024 and 2025.
  • Policies Status: The report showed that at present, 87 carbon policies are being implemented globally, increasing by 7 since 2025, with India, and Viet Nam actively developing them.The report highlighted that if all carbon pricing policies under development are implemented by 2030, then, nearly1/3rd (33.33%) of global GHG emissions could come under carbon pricing systems.

11.14  MoH&FW releases the 10th NHA estimates for FY23; GHE jumps to Rs 3.85 lakh Crp.220
Exam Hints:
  • What: MoH&FW releases NHA estimates for FY23
  • Purpose: Insights into pattern of health expenditure
  • Prepared by: NHATs, NHSRC, MoH&FW
  • Total Health Expenditure (THE): Rs 8.81 lakh Cr, 3.37% of GDP
  • Government Health Expenditure (GHE): 1.48% of GDP
  • GHE in GGE: 4.89%
  • GHE in THE: 43.7% in 2022-23
  • Per Capita: Rs 2786 in 2022-23
  • Current Health Expenditure (CHE): CG- Rs 88,721 Cr, SG- Rs 1.62 Lakh Cr, Household- Rs 4.32 Cr
  • Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE): 43.4% in 2022-23
  • Social Security Expenditure (SSE): 9.2%
Background:
  • The report highlighted that Government Health Expenditure (GHE) increased from Rs 1.30 lakh crore (Cr) in 2013-14 to Rs 3.85 lakh Cr in 2022-23, stating higher public investment in the health sector.
Key Highlights:
  • Government Health Expenditure (GHE): The share of GHE in the country’s GDP (base year:2022-23) has risen from 1.15% in 2013–14 to 1.43% in 2022–23.GHE’s share in General Government Expenditure (GGE) has increased from 3.78% to 4.89% over the same period.In per capita terms, GHE has increased nearly 2.7 times, from Rs. 1,042 to Rs. 2,786 between 2013-14 and 2022-23.
  • Rising GHE: The share of GHE in THE has increased by almost 15%, from 28.6% in 2013-14 to 43.7% in 2022–23.
  • Current Health Expenditure (CHE): Of the CHE, the CG’s share is Rs 88,721 Cr (11.57% of CHE) and SG’s share is Rs 1.62 lakh Cr (21.22% of CHE) and household’s share is (including insurance contributions) about Rs 4.32 Cr (56.44% of CHE).

About Loktak Protocluster:
  • Loktak Lake: The largest freshwater lake in Northeast India, famous for its floating “phumdis” masses of vegetation, soil, and organic matter drifting on water.
  • Timeline: It is located about 12.6 billion light-years away in the direction of the constellation Sextans, allowing us to observe it as it existed when the Universe was only about 1.2 billion years old (around 9% of its current age).
  • Collaboration: The discovery was made by combining data from Japan’s Subaru Telescope, Hawaii, United States of America (USA), and NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), USA using wide-field and high-resolution infrared observations.
  • Impact: The study shows that “cosmic environments” influenced early galaxy evolution, with galaxies in dense regions like the Loktak Protocluster evolving differently and appearing about 1.4 times larger due to strong interactions.

Key Details of Findings:
  • Evidence: A 1.1 kilo meter(km) crater in the Faustini Basin showed strong evidence of lunar ice, with radar signals and lobate-rim features indicating impact into an ice-rich subsurface that briefly flowed and refroze.The study examined ‘doubly shadowed craters’ within the Moon’s Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs).
  • Detection Method: The discovery was made using the Dual-Frequency Synthetic Aperture Radar (DFSAR), operates at L- and S-band frequencies, onboard Chandrayaan-2, capable of penetrating the Moon’s surface and mapping subsurface structures.
  • Chandrayaan-2: Launched in July 2019, Chandrayaan-2 is India’s second lunar exploration mission developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), aimed at enhancing scientific understanding of the Moon and generating important lunar data.

20.2  International Workers’ Day 2026 – May 1p.316
Exam Hints:
  • What: International Workers’ Day 2026
  • Also Called (India): May Day / Antar Rashtriya Shramik Divas / Kamgar Din
  • When: May 1, 2026
  • Purpose: Honour workers; promote fair wages & labour rights
  • Origin: Haymarket Affair (1886, Chicago)
  • Global Recognition: 1889 – Second International declared May 1
  • India First Observed: 1923 – Chennai (then Madras).
Background:
  • In India, International Workers’ Day is known as ‘May Day’, ‘Antar Rashtriya Shramik Divas’, and ‘Kamgar Din’.
Background:
  • Origin: The day traces back to the Haymarket Affair on May 4, 1886, when a peaceful rally demanding an eight-hour workday turned violent after a bomb explosion, marking a defining moment in the global struggle for workers’ rights.
  • Global Recognition: In 1889, the Second International declared May 1 as International Workers’ Day to commemorate the Haymarket Affair and to advance labor rights worldwide.
  • Observance in India: In India, the day was first observed on May 1, 1923, in Chennai (then Madras) by the Labour Kisan Party of Hindustan under the leadership of Malayapuram Singaravelu Chettiar, marking the beginning of the organized labor movement in the country.
Eight-Hour Day Movement:
  • 1919 Convention: This led to the adoption of the Hours of Work (Industry) Convention, 1919, which established the eight-hour workday as an international standard.

Director-General (DG): Gilbert F. Houngbo
Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland
Established: 1919

Global Progress:
  • Rising Sustainability: In 2017, only 75% of tuna catches came from healthy, non-overfished stocks; today, about 99% of commercial tuna catches are sourced from stocks assessed as biologically sustainable by the UN.
  • Stock Recovery: Of 23 major tuna stocks, only 2 remain overfished, a significant decline from 13 stocks in 2014.
Global Initiative:
  • Project: In 2022, the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), launched the Common Oceans Tuna Project to ensure all major tuna stocks are sustainably fished by 2027.
  • Scope: The project, formally titled Sustainable Management of Tuna Fisheries and Biodiversity Conservation in the Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction (ABNJ Tuna Project), builds on earlier efforts from 2014–2019.

22.1  ZSI Discovers Two New Spider Species in Nagaland; Revises Indian Whip Scorpions After a Centuryp.384
Exam Hints:
  • What: Discovery of two new spider species
  • New Spider Species: Psechrus ntu and Psechrus phenshunyu
  • Discovered by: ZSI
  • Where: Nagaland
  • Published in: Zootaxa
  • Whip Scorpions: ‘Thelyphonids’ known as Vinegaroons
Background:
  • The findings were published in the International Journal Zootaxa.
About New Spider Species:
  • Discovery: The newly discovered spider species were named after Ntu and Phenshunyu villages in Nagaland, highlighting Northeast India as a biodiversity hotspot.
  • Species: Both species belong to the genus Psechrus under the family Psechridae and Psechrus himalayanus was recorded in the region for the first time.
  • Features: The spiders possess elongated and dorsoventrally flattened bodies, long anterior legs, sensory hairs for vibration detection, and construct large horizontal sheet webs in humid forest habitats.
About Whip Scorpions:
  • Features: Whip Scorpions, or Vinegaroons, are non-venomous arachnids distinct from true scorpions, characterised by whip-like tails (flagella), enlarged pedipalps for catching prey, and acetic acid-like defensive spray mechanisms.
  • Distribution: These nocturnal and burrowing arachnids are adapted to humid forest ecosystems and are found in India’s eastern border regions near Bangladesh, Myanmar, and China.

22.2  New Worm-Eating Snake ‘Trachischium lalremsangai’ Discovered in Mizoramp.385
Exam Hints:
  • What: New worm-eating snake species discovered
  • Name of Species: Trachischium lalremsangai
  • Where: Mizoram and Myanmar
  • Named After: Dr. H.T. Lalremsanga (Mizoram University Herpetologist)
  • Genus: Trachischium
  • Published in: International Journal Herpetozoa.
Background:
  • The species was named after Hmar Tlawmte Lalremsanga, Professor of Zoology at Mizoram University, in recognition of his contributions to herpetology research in India.
  • The discovery was formally documented in the international journal Herpetozoa, published by the Austrian Herpetological Society.
About Trachischium lalremsangai:
  • Habitat: The species is small, non-venomous, and harmless snakes that live underground (semi-fossorial), found in loose soil, leaf litter, and forest debris. commonly known as slender snakes or worm-eating snakes.
  • Identification: It is identified by its smooth, iridescent scales, two postocular scales behind the eye, and a light brown to white-speckled belly, distinguishing it from related species that have dark brown or black undersides.
  • Classification: It marks the 11th recognized species of the Trachischium genus found in Northeast India and the Himalayan region.
